correctness.rationale: The backward two-state telegraph hitting equations yield the unique bounded exponential solutions with q=sqrt[r(r+2 alpha)]/v and c=exp(-arcosh(1+r/alpha)). Restarting at the first Poisson clock gives exact bulk adsorption means (1-F)/(rF) and (1-C)/(rF); geometric wall cycles then give M_W-M_H=Gamma(1-C/F)/r, eliminating the common wall dwell law. For inward home orientation, the phase boundary is beta=theta/sinh(theta); strict monotonicity of theta/sinh(theta) and theta tanh(theta/2) proves both rate-section uniqueness results. Taylor and exponential expansions prove the exact endpoint laws. A standalone checker passed 923 deterministic and simulated checks. Assumptions 0<p<1, finite mean dwell, alpha/r/v/u positive, independent wall choices are indispensable; computation is not used as an infinite-family proof.

value.rationale: The parent paper deliberately asks which desorption mechanism minimizes mean capture and provides qualitative contours. The new necessary-and-sufficient curve settles the full parameter-choice problem with no hidden extra crossings, treats both initial directions, quantifies how preferred regimes narrow at small tumble intensity or high resetting, and proves robustness under arbitrary common finite-mean wall waiting laws. This natural complete phase classification supplies experimentally interpretable design guidance beyond a parameter-specific contour, although it is a targeted analytical sharpening of established formulas rather than a broad new physical framework.
